9.0.s.en: (1) Paul urges the Corinthians to give

9.0.0.en: The ministering: collecting gifts for the poor.

9.0.1.en: The saints: those sanctified in Christ, that is, the believers, and he means the poor Christians in Jerusalem. This is different from the title we give to those who have reached a high degree in the spiritual life, whom we call saints. Superfluous: excessive talk.

9.0.2.en: Paul encourages the Corinthians to collect gifts for the poor of Jerusalem, and affirms their concern for this, and in a gentle manner says that his words are superfluous but he means them only as a reminder.

9.1.0.en: Your forwardness of mind: your concern to offer gifts for the poor.

9.1.1.en: They of Macedonia: the believers in the northern part of Greece.

9.1.2.en: Achaia: the southern part of Greece, whose capital is Corinth, and here he means the believers in Corinth.

9.1.3.en: Paul commends the Christians in Corinth, because their concern for collecting donations encouraged the other churches to do so, although they had not yet collected anything, but when they heard last year of this need they declared their readiness to take part in it. This is a gentle approach by Paul when urging them to collect gifts, to commend them first, since he found in them a heartfelt concern, even if they had not expressed it by an actual collection of gifts.

9.2.0.en: The brethren: Titus and his two companions.

9.2.1.en: The boldness of boasting: Paul's boldness in boasting of the Corinthians in their concern for collecting the gifts. Paul sent Titus and the servants with him to encourage the Church of Corinth and collect the donations, and he expects some believers from Macedonia to accompany him, so he encourages them by this epistle to collect the gifts so that his boasting of their concern in this matter may be justified, and so that they do not put him to shame, and put themselves to shame, if they were slack and were content with readiness in words and did nothing.

9.3.0.en: Paul sent Titus and his two companions to collect the donations before he himself arrived with some Christians from the churches of Macedonia, for it was the custom that some believers accompanied him on his journeys, so that when he arrived the collection would be complete. He calls these gifts a blessing, not only for the one who receives but also for the one who gives, because he gave to Christ. His intention in this was that the Corinthians should not fall short, having collected little and not completed the whole collection, and do it in his presence before the Macedonians, so that their shortcoming and stinginess would appear. So he wants the collection to be completed by Titus before he arrives with the Macedonians.

9.3.1.en: When you ask something of someone or reproach him for some mistake, may you begin your words with praise, for this makes the other ready to accept your words and even to rejoice in them.

9.4.0.en: Paul calls the Corinthians to give generously, drawing on what happens in farming. He who sows few seeds reaps a small harvest from them, but he who sows bountifully, that is, with abundance of seed, reaps a large harvest. Likewise he who gives little to the needy, God grants him few blessings in his life, but he who gives generously, God's blessings to him are many.

9.5.0.en: Grudgingly: he gives but is troubled when he gives, because he loves money and is attached to it.

9.5.1.en: Of necessity: he is embarrassed before the one who asks him, or ashamed before those around him, so he gives but not out of love.

9.5.2.en: Here the Apostle calls believers to give cheerfully, for the gift of each one must be given with love so that God's heart may rejoice. Paul cited a verse with this meaning from the Book of Proverbs (Prov 22:9) as in the Septuagint.

9.6.0.en: The Apostle promises the one who gives that God will reward him with many graces and provide for his material needs in everything and at every time, that is, always. And when his material needs are supplied, he is free to care for spiritual growth and for increasing works of goodness. The Church has taken up this verse in the Divine Liturgy in the Litany of the Plants, the Airs of Heaven and the Waters of the Rivers.

9.7.0.en: The Apostle affirms his words about God's blessings to the one who gives, for He helps him so that he keeps giving throughout his life and therefore lives in righteousness, not only on earth but also in the Kingdom forever. He cited the Book of Psalms (Ps 112:9).

9.8.0.en: The Apostle reassures those who give that they will not become poor and needy, because God, who gives the whole world, both seed to the farmer so that he may sow it and food to the hungry, is Himself able to give to those who give to the needy not only material gifts but also righteousness and the spiritual life with Him.

9.9.0.en: Paul shows that God's gifts to those who give generously are sufficient for them and enrich them, and this makes Paul and all the believers thank God: 1- for His gifts to the one who gives; 2- that He put into the heart of the one who gives a concern for others; 3- for supplying the needs of the needy.

9.10.0.en: The administration of this service: carrying out the collection of the gifts.

9.10.1.en: Here Paul affirms that collecting the gifts not only supplies the needs of the poor in Jerusalem but also increases prayers of thanksgiving to God, so the life of the believers grows.

9.11.1.en: The experiment of this ministration: when they receive the gifts from the Corinthians.

9.11.2.en: Your professed subjection: your obedience, you believers who confess Christ.

9.11.3.en: The Apostle shows the feelings of the believers in Jerusalem when they receive these gifts, so they thank God for two things:

9.11.4.en: 1- The existence of many believers in the world who obey the Gospel and offer gifts out of love for God.

9.11.5.en: 2- The many gifts which they receive in abundance.

9.12.0.en: The Apostle continues the feelings of the believers in Jerusalem when they receive the gifts, and they do two things:

9.12.1.en: 1- They pray for you, believers of Corinth.

9.12.2.en: 2- They long to see them, as they feel their fellowship with them in the body of Christ, that is, the one Church.

9.13.0.en: Finally Paul thanks God for His grace, which is first faith in Christ and the work of the Holy Spirit, who stirs up love in the hearts of the believers so that they give gifts to the needy.

9.13.1.en: If you look at God's gifts to you, given generously and with fatherly love, your heart will be moved to care for everyone around you, and you will give with joy and give generously.

9.13.2.en: The authority of St. Paul the Apostle

10.0.s.en: (1) Paul's authority over those who oppose him

10.0.0.en: St. Paul speaks with meekness like the meek Christ, and says to the Corinthians that he was an ordinary, weak man when he preached to them, and they received his gentle words, but now in the epistle he appears strong and speaks with authority. The truth is that Paul was not weak, but he humbled himself in meekness during his preaching, and then those who oppose him rose up against him, provoking him to come among them, and they interpreted his delay in coming as fear and weakness to face them, although it is not so. As a bishop and spiritual head over them he has his authority, whether among them or when he sends them an epistle, and the concerns of the ministry are what keep him from coming.

10.1.0.en: Be bold: act with authority and severity.

10.1.1.en: Some: the false teachers who oppose Paul.

10.1.2.en: As if we walked according to the flesh: acting according to the evil desires of the flesh and not as spiritual people.

10.1.3.en: Paul wishes that when he comes to Corinth he will not find opposition and errors from the false teachers who influence the believers, so that he will not be compelled to use his spiritual authority to punish the offenders, even if those who oppose him interpret these actions of his as mistaken human behavior, that is, that he became angry and out of his anger issues commands and punishments.

10.2.0.en: Paul declares that although he is a man who lives in the flesh, that is, eats and drinks and sleeps like the rest of human beings, he does not wage war in his spiritual striving and ministry in a human way, that is, with passions and desires and pride, but walks in a spiritual way.

10.3.0.en: Paul declares that the weapons with which he fights are spiritual and not carnal, those he mentioned in (Eph 6:11-16), and they are strong weapons able to pull down the strongholds of evil in which the people who oppose the work of God walk.

10.4.0.en: Every high thing: in ancient times they built strongholds on high places. Here the Apostle likens the pride of those who oppose to these high strongholds.

10.4.2.en: Paul speaks with confidence in God and in his spiritual weapons, that they are able to remove the evil imaginations that those who oppose stir up in the midst of the Church to disturb it, and to overcome their pride and draw souls to faith and obedience to the commandments of Christ, so that they become captive to His love.

10.5.0.en: The Apostle reassures the believers in Corinth that if they submit to him in the obedience of children, they need not be troubled by those who oppose, who cause problems within the Church, for he is able by the power of God to avenge, that is, to punish them in order to stop their evils and so that they repent.

10.5.1.en: Be gentle and show your love to others, but do not give up the truth; rather proclaim it. Also, if you have responsibility as a parent or a superior, use your authority to prevent evil for God's sake, and not as human anger or for private purposes.

10.6.0.en: Paul addresses those who oppose and says to them, if you look at me as a weak man when I was present with you, I declare to you that if you believe in Christ, be confident that I have the same faith and power. For some of them claimed distinction because they had seen Christ in the flesh, or because of a distant bodily kinship with Jesus.

10.7.0.en: In the previous verse, Paul showed that he is no less in his faith in Christ than those who oppose him in the Church of Corinth. Here he declares his distinction from them by his authority as head and the one responsible for the Church, and his boasting and holding to this authority is for the edification of the Church and not for its destruction like these who oppose. He is not ashamed to declare this authority because he received it from Christ when He called him, and he uses it for His glory.

10.8.0.en: Here Paul repels the charge of these who oppose him, that he frightens the believers in Corinth by his epistles. The truth is that what he says is not a threat but real authority from God that he can use if these who oppose persist in their evil.

10.9.0.en: Paul denounces the words of those who oppose, who claim that Paul's epistles are strong and firm, but if Paul himself comes to Corinth his weakness will appear. This, of course, is a false statement and mere claims of those who oppose, to disturb the Church and spread false ideas.

10.10.0.en: Here Paul declares the truth, which is that he has authority and is strong, both in his epistles and when he visits the Church of Corinth.

10.11.0.en: We dare not: we do not allow ourselves to claim authority that is not ours.

10.11.1.en: Measuring themselves by themselves: that is, they praise themselves and do not compare themselves with the Fathers and the first teachers so as to learn from them.

10.11.2.en: Paul refuses to commend himself like these who oppose, who deceived themselves by praising themselves and strayed from measuring themselves by the truth, and so went astray.

10.12.0.en: Things without our measure: claiming authority or gifts that are not in us.

10.12.1.en: The measure of the rule which God hath distributed to us: that is, the authority and gifts that God gave us. To reach even unto you: to preach to you and care for you, since as a bishop he is responsible for them before God. Paul affirms that he does not claim any authority or gifts that are not his, as these who oppose do, but uses his authority and gifts to serve and preach to the Corinthians, that they may believe and live with Christ.

10.13.0.en: We stretch not ourselves: we do not claim that we preached to you when we did not preach to you, or claim an imaginary authority over you.

10.13.1.en: Paul affirms that he is the one who preached and founded the Church in Corinth, so he does not claim a false authority over them, but he is the one who came and preached among them as an apostle of Christ, a bishop and head over His Church.

10.14.0.en: Things without our measure, that is, other men's labors: that is, what others did of preachers and servants.

10.14.1.en: Enlarged by you: our ministry and work among you increase.

10.14.2.en: The Apostle affirms that he does not claim for himself works he did not do and which were done before him, as those who oppose do, who came to Corinth after Paul founded the Church there and left it, and claimed that they were the founders of the Church. Rather, Paul was careful to preach in places where none of the other Apostles had preached. He hopes that the Corinthians will grow in their faith so that they give him the opportunity for his ministry among them to increase, and he may even turn some of them into servants who help him in preaching to the countries around them. All this he will do according to the rule given to him by God, that is, the gifts that the Holy Spirit grants him.

10.15.0.en: In the regions beyond you: west of Corinth, that is, Rome and Spain.

10.15.1.en: Another man's line: the places where other apostles and preachers preached.

10.15.2.en: Paul continues his wishes, that if the believers in Corinth help him by their steadfastness and spiritual growth, he will not be hindered by their problems, but will care for ministering and preaching in the other regions where no one has preached, and founding churches for Christ.

10.16.0.en: Here the Apostle sets down an important spiritual truth, which is not to boast in honor or human achievements, but in God's pleasure and delight in us, and our faith and our enjoyment of His care.

10.17.0.en: The Apostle therefore affirms that God's commendation of a person is what approves him, and not that he become proud and commend himself. God's commendation appears in the virtues and spiritual fruits that He gives to His children and in His support of them in their spiritual striving and their service.

10.17.1.en: Do not be preoccupied with honor and people's praise of you, and do not slip into praising yourself, but care for positive work in knowing God and being joined to Him and, on the other hand, in loving others and helping them, and God's blessings will overflow upon you and you will thank Him, and this will drive you to continual positive work.

10.17.2.en: Paul's defense of his apostleship and his ministry

11.0.0.en: The Apostle forbade anyone to praise himself like the false teachers who oppose him, and counts this as ignorance and folly, because praise should come from God. But here he is compelled to praise himself in order to establish his apostleship and therefore the teachings he preached to the Corinthians. Because what appears is self-praise, he said to them, bear with me in my folly. He commends them that they were originally distinguished by the virtue of forbearance, and because they love him they will bear with him.

11.1.0.en: I am jealous over you: I love you and refuse that you should stray into evil and false teachings, so that you remain in your sound faith, and my love makes me weary if I see you attached to the world and not to Christ. With godly jealousy: for the glory of God and not for a personal purpose.

11.1.1.en: I have espoused you: I preached to you and you believed and were joined, as a bride to her heavenly Bridegroom, Christ.

11.1.2.en: Paul shows his love for the Church of Corinth in that he grieves and is distressed if they turn away from Christ, because by his preaching to them he joined them to Him as a bride, so they must remain in purity like a virgin betrothed to her bridegroom, Christ.

11.2.0.en: Paul continues to show his feelings toward the Church of Corinth, for which he fears lest it be deceived by the ideas of the false teachers, as Satan in the form of the serpent deceived our mother Eve of old. So he asks them to remain in the simplicity of the faith and to beware of the craftiness of the wicked who oppose.

11.3.0.en: Another Jesus: other than Jesus Christ, the Son of the Virgin Mary.

11.3.1.en: Another spirit: other than the Holy Spirit.

11.3.2.en: Another gospel: other than the Gospel that Paul preached, which declares that Jesus Christ is God. Paul supposes the existence of teachers who teach another Jesus and another Holy Spirit and another gospel, confirming their teachings with them and with miracles that establish them. All this might be a strong deception that leads the Corinthians away from the faith, so that they would have an acceptable excuse. But the false teachers did not proclaim this; rather they confuse them with strange ideas for the sake of their pride, so why do they follow them? It would have been better for them to hold fast to the sound teaching that Paul preached and reject the ideas of those who oppose.

11.4.0.en: The very chiefest apostles: the foremost Apostles, who are Peter, James and John, whom Christ singled out for certain occasions such as the Transfiguration.

11.4.1.en: Those who oppose cast doubt on Paul's apostleship, and here he defends it in order also to establish the teachings he taught them, so he declares that he is not only an apostle because Christ appeared to him and entrusted everything to him, but is in no way inferior to the Apostles counted as pillars, because of his labors in the ministry and the gifts God gave him. And his bringing the Gentiles into the faith does not diminish his apostleship, as those who oppose accuse him, but establishes it.

11.5.0.en: Perhaps some of those who oppose accused Paul of weakness in oratory in Greek because he had not studied in the famous Greek schools, although in truth he is distinguished by his eloquence. So Paul defends himself, declaring: even if you judged that I am weak in oratory, that is, common, yet in knowledge and spiritual understanding I am not weak, because I learned everything from Christ directly. This knowledge of mine appeared through my preaching among you and in every place where I preached. Perhaps preaching in the vernacular was a necessity in many cases to explain theological truths to simple people, and this does not diminish the depth of the speaker in any way.

11.5.1.en: Defend yourself for God's sake and so that you do not cause others to stumble, but let your defense not be for the sake of your honor or to justify your mistakes; rather be humble and apologize for your mistakes, and you will be strong and win the love of those around you.

11.6.0.en: I abased myself: I endured providing for my living expenses by the work of my hands.

11.6.1.en: That ye might be exalted: that you might be joined and grow in the knowledge of God, not occupied with providing for the expenses of me and those with me, so that my free ministry may encourage you to be bound to the love of Christ.

11.6.2.en: Paul declared the Apostle's right to take his living expenses from those he serves (1 Cor 9:6-12), and those who oppose objected to his apostleship because he does not receive his living expenses from those he serves, so he answered them that he has the right to take these expenses but he gave them up so as not to hinder them from their attachment to Christ and His love.

11.7.0.en: I robbed: I accepted gifts from other churches for your ministry, although the believers in Corinth could have provided his expenses, but out of love he did not burden them, so he provided for his needs from the work of his hands and from the donations of other churches.

11.7.1.en: Other churches: the churches of Macedonia (v. 9), and especially the Church of Philippi.

11.7.2.en: The Apostle adds, in not burdening the Church of Corinth in providing his expenses, that he supplied his needs from the donations of other churches, and he rose above being a burdensome guest to anyone.

11.8.0.en: This boasting: the free ministry in Corinth.

11.8.1.en: Shall stop me: no one will prevent me from it.

11.8.2.en: Achaia: the southern region of Greece whose capital is Corinth.

11.8.3.en: Paul affirms the truth of his words in Christ, who taught him truthfulness, that no member of this Church can stop him from his boasting that he served the Church of Corinth free of charge, or reproach him for it, because it is clear before everyone.

11.9.0.en: Paul asks why he did not take his expenses from the Church of Corinth: was it because he did not love them?.. Of course not. And he affirms his words by saying that God knows the measure of his love for them.

11.10.0.en: He adds that he will continue to serve the Church of Corinth free of charge so that those who oppose may not find anything against him, that he serves for material gain. For as they tear down Paul's standing, they gain standing and power. The false teachers perhaps perform their teaching free of charge and boast of it, and therefore Paul is careful to serve free of charge so that these who oppose may not use that as a reason to accuse him of wanting material gain.

11.11.0.en: Paul exposes the evil of those who oppose him in Corinth, describing them as not true apostles but false, and as crafty, deceiving the simple by their false teachings. Christ did not send them; they only claim it.

11.12.0.en: The Apostle goes on to expose those who oppose and to reveal their pretending to be sent by Christ, just as their chief does, Satan, who can appear in the form of an angel of light although he is a devil and his conduct is entirely the opposite of the angels. And because they are servants of Satan, it is no strange thing that they imitate him in deceiving people by pretending to be apostles of Christ, but God will repay them for their evil works with eternal torment if they do not repent.

11.12.1.en: Offer your love to those around you freely, and do not ask for a material return, and even if they fall short in appreciating your labors or wrong you with words of rebuke and insult, do not give up your love for them. And if you cannot offer them love, at least pray for them.

11.13.s.en: (3) Paul's being compelled to praise himself

11.13.0.en: Paul was compelled to praise himself in order to establish his apostleship, so he says to the Corinthians, do not think that this is folly on my part when I praise myself, for I do not seek any special honor for myself, but I do this for the confirmation of your faith when I establish my apostleship. And even if you think this is folly, bear with me and listen to me as you listened to the false teachers when they praised themselves although they are not apostles of Christ.

11.14.0.en: That which I speak: that is, what Paul defended his apostleship with, which appeared in the form of boasting.

11.14.1.en: After the Lord: not like the humble Christ, who did not praise Himself.

11.14.2.en: As it were foolishly: it appears to be ignorance and folly.

11.14.3.en: The confidence of boasting: boldness in praising himself.

11.14.4.en: Paul declares that the opposition of the false teachers is what compelled him to praise himself to establish his apostleship. This is not the way Christ followed and asks His disciples to follow, but it is a special case that compelled him to it. It appears to be folly and needless boldness, but whoever looks closely will know that this is for the confirmation of the faith of the Church of Corinth.

11.15.1.en: After the flesh: that is, they are Jews and circumcised and adhere to the Law.

11.15.2.en: The reason for Paul's boasting is that the false teachers boasted in vain of fleshly things in order to draw people to their false teachings. So Paul was compelled to boast, but for a sound reason, which is to confirm the teachings of Christ that He told him.

11.16.0.en: Paul commends the Corinthians as being wise and as having borne with the folly of the false teachers in their boasting, so let them complete their forbearance by listening to Paul's defense even if they think it foolish talk. It is wisdom on Paul's part to draw them to listen to him by praising them and by his humility, describing himself as though he were a fool, although in truth the Corinthians were fools in being led after the teachings of those who oppose and giving up the teachings of Paul who preached to them.

11.17.0.en: Bringeth you into bondage: to the Mosaic ordinances found in the laws of the Law, when they imposed them on them after they became Christians.

11.17.2.en: Take of you: lords it over you and takes you as prey that he exploits.

11.17.3.en: Exalt himself: is proud toward you and humbles you.

11.17.4.en: Smite you on the face: all kinds of insults.

11.17.5.en: Paul says to the Corinthians, you bore with the false teachers, who enslaved you to the customs of the Law and exploited you and insulted you, so bear with me in my praise of myself.

11.18.0.en: By way of reproach: the insults that Paul endured.

11.18.1.en: We have been weak: in humility Paul describes himself and those with him as weak, or those who oppose used to describe them as weak.

11.18.2.en: Wherein any is bold: the boasting of those who oppose about themselves.

11.18.3.en: Paul declares that he endured appearing in a guise of weakness and humiliation for the sake of preaching the Gospel of Christ, but now he is compelled to show his strength by praising himself in order to establish his apostleship in the face of false claims and the false teachers' praise of themselves.

11.18.4.en: Endure insults for God's sake, and defend yourself also for His sake and not to show your honor or out of anger within you and pride. That is, do what you wish, but for one purpose, the glorification of God and not the glorification of yourself.

11.19.s.en: (4) The kinds of labors that Paul endured in his ministry

11.19.0.en: Paul declares that he is no less than the false teachers in his lineage.

11.19.1.en: Hebrews: named after "Eber," one of the forefathers of "Abraham," or after Abraham, who crossed the Euphrates River to the land of Canaan, so Abraham is called a Hebrew (Gen 14:13) and his descendants Hebrews.

11.19.2.en: Israelites: named after Israel, who is Jacob, and the meaning of Israel is that he strove with God and prevailed (Gen 32:28), that is, they are God's own people.

11.19.3.en: The seed of Abraham: who received the promises from God, so they are heirs of these promises, especially since from them comes Christ the Savior.

11.20.0.en: I am more: the false teachers claim to be servants of Christ, but Paul is in truth a servant of God in love and humility, and God sent him to preach, so he is not a forger or a pretender, and therefore he is more. In labours: for the sake of the ministry.

11.20.1.en: In deaths: his frequent exposure to death.

11.20.2.en: In this verse Paul shows not only his equality with the false teachers in lineage but also his distinction from them in the ministry, both in the abundance of his labors and his enduring beating and scourging and being thrown into prisons and, more than this, his exposure to death many times.

11.21.0.en: Forty stripes save one: the Law of Moses decreed that the scourging should not exceed forty, so they were accustomed to strike 39 lest they fall into error. And the whip had three thongs, so each stroke was counted as three, that is, he is struck 13 times.

11.21.1.en: Beaten with rods: most likely by the Romans.

11.21.2.en: Once was I stoned: that was at Lystra, and he lost consciousness (Acts 14:19). Thrice I suffered shipwreck: this is not mentioned in the Book of Acts, and a fourth time is mentioned that happened after the writing of this epistle when he was going to Rome (Acts 27:41). In the deep: when he was clinging to one of the planks of wood in the sea and spent long hours, whether at night or by day, until God saved him, and this happened in the case of his shipwreck three times. Paul shows some of the labors he endured in his ministry and by which he was distinguished from the false teachers, such as scourging, beating, stoning, shipwreck and his clinging to its planks in the sea.

11.22.0.en: In journeyings: bearing the pain and hardships of travel in his moving between many countries, noting that the means of transport were primitive and so involved much suffering.

11.22.1.en: Perils of waters: heavy rains that fall on some countries and may cost the lives of many whom they sweep away in their path.

11.22.2.en: Perils of robbers: highwaymen who attack travelers to seize what they have, so that travelers are exposed to being killed.

11.22.3.en: Perils by mine own countrymen: that is, the Jews who opposed him, whether in Jerusalem or in the various countries of the world in which he preached.

11.22.4.en: Perils by the heathen: those among whom he preached in the whole world, and who stirred up many against him to kill him.

11.22.5.en: Perils in the city: that is, the cities in which he preached and they rose against him and beat him and tried to kill him.

11.22.6.en: Perils in the wilderness: the deserts he passed through during his missionary journeys.

11.22.7.en: Perils in the sea: where he traveled by sea in ships many times, and the ships were primitive and were wrecked more than once, and he was exposed to drowning.

11.22.8.en: Perils among false brethren: the false teachers, who are the Jews who became Christians and opposed his teachings because he showed that the Mosaic customs were a type of Christianity, so there is no need to hold to most of them.

11.22.9.en: The Apostle showed some of the suffering he met in his ministry that exposed him to death, and this shows his love for God and his worthiness to be called an apostle and servant of the Corinthians more than the false teachers.

11.23.0.en: In watchings: Paul's keeping vigil while preaching and teaching, and also in the work of his hands to provide for his living expenses. In hunger and thirst: he endured at times, during his preaching, extreme poverty, as he did not find his necessary food. In fastings: which he fasted and joined with prayers for his ministry, whether the fasts that the Apostles decreed for the whole Church or additional fasts to seek God's help.

11.23.1.en: In cold and nakedness: because he was exposed to extreme poverty, so he did not find what would clothe him and warm him while preaching in countries with a cold climate.

11.23.2.en: The Apostle continues the troubles he bore in his ministry, showing his perseverance in enduring the labors of the ministry and poverty and his need of necessary food and clothing, in addition to fasts, that God might have compassion on him.

11.24.0.en: Paul mentions that what was mentioned above is some of the sufferings, and there are many other labors, lesser than these sufferings, such as his care for the churches in which he preached, as well as the organization of the ministry and following it up.

11.25.0.en: Who is weak: is tired physically or is affected spiritually.

11.25.1.en: And I am not weak: I pity him and am affected by his weakness, that is, my heart is moved toward him.

11.25.2.en: Is offended: turns away from the faith.

11.25.3.en: And I burn not: that is, my heart is filled with zeal and jealousy to rescue him and support him.

11.25.4.en: Paul makes clear that all the labors mentioned above he went through not only as bodily sufferings, but he was affected psychologically by the sins and falls and deviation from God of many of the believers, so he is zealous to exhort them and show his love for them in order to bring them back to the Church.

11.26.0.en: The false teachers boasted of their knowledge, their eloquence and their lineage, but Paul boasted of his labors and what he endured for the sake of Christ, since it is the proof of his love; and this confirms that he is a true servant.

11.27.0.en: Paul calls God Himself as witness to the truth of his previous words so that they may trust what he says to them.

11.28.0.en: Damascus: an ancient well-known city in Syria.

11.28.1.en: Governor: the ruler of the city.

11.28.2.en: Aretas: a title of the kings of the Arabs and of Syria, like Pharaoh for the kings of Egypt.

11.28.3.en: Kept the city of the Damascenes: watched the gates in order to seize Paul if he tried to escape, because the Jews stirred him up against him.

11.28.4.en: A window: an opening in a house adjoining the wall.

11.28.5.en: A basket: a large basket, that is, a large carrying basket.

11.28.6.en: It seems that this incident was dangerous and Paul's death in it was almost certain, so he mentioned it separately and showed God's protection of him, for he was able to escape from the city while the governor's soldiers were trying to seize him. He went out let down in a basket and went on walking alone in the wilderness until he reached another city.

11.28.7.en: Look at the love of Christ and what He endured on the cross for your sake, so that you are moved to give yourself for everyone around you and serve with all your strength, confident of God's support and care for you.

11.28.8.en: Paul's vision, his weakness and his establishing his apostleship
